No recreational crabbing on Wednesdays, except private-property pots, handlines and dip nets, or in a week with a state/federal holiday on Wed or Thu. Still in effect per guide updated Aug 2026.

Trotlines, seines, eel pots (bait), collapsible traps or net rings if 16+, or keeping more than the unlicensed limit.
Handlines, dip nets, under-16 using traps/rings, helping a licensee, aboard a boat showing a crab boat decal, up to 2 registered waterfront pots.
MD resident $5; with Bay sport fishing or senior license $2; non-resident $10; valid 365 days.
$15 decal on forward half of hull (either side); covers everyone aboard; includes a free individual license for use off the boat.
Unlimited, no license.
Licensed only. Max 1,200 ft of baited line (first bait to last). Max 1,200 ft per boat no matter how many licensees.
Licensed: up to 30 total (traps + rings combined). Guide says gear amount is per boat, not per person (check DNR).
Collapsible trap: flat bottom max 20 x 15 in., max 4 sides, must close only when you pull the line (auto-closing 'Crab Alert' traps illegal). Net ring: max 30 in. diameter, mesh max 1/4 in.
Don't set a trotline, trap or ring within 100 ft of someone else's set gear. Never fish another person's gear.
Owners/lessees/tenants of private shoreline: max 2 pots per property. Free annual DNR registration (not a license; unlicensed limits apply).
In front of the property, within 100 yards of shore; tied to the property or marked by buoy/pole and sign.
Turtle reduction device in each lower-chamber entrance, max 1 3/4 x 4 3/4 in. Two cull rings: one at least 2 3/16 in., one at least 2 5/16 in. Marked with your DNRid.
Buoy each end, same color/size/shape; spherical 12 in.+ diameter (or 12x10x10 in.); show your DNRid.
Buoy with your DNRid unless the trap is tied to a pier, wharf or boat.

regs.va: Virginia differs a lot: no license for dip nets, handlines or up to 2 crab pots; licenses ($6-$46) cover a 300 ft trotline (Apr 15-Oct 15) or 3-5 pots (Jun 1-Sep 15, no 3-5 pots on Sundays). Limit is 1 bushel hard crabs and 2 dozen peelers per person per day. Male and immature female hard crabs 5 in.; mature females may be kept with no size limit (MD bans all females). Bright-orange sponge crabs only Mar 17-Jun 15; release all sponges recommended. Pots out of the water Dec 1-Mar 16; lower-Bay blue crab sanctuaries closed in summer. Buoys marked 'R' + last 4 of license/SSN number. VMRC page last updated July 2025 and the crab regulation was amended July 5, 2026 (check VMRC).

steps: Get a MD crab license (or boat decal) first; trotlines need one.
Rig: main line (5/32 in. Dacron or 3-strand nylon), 2-3 ft chain at each end, then ~20 ft line to a buoy and ~20 ft to the anchor.
Snoods: ~6 in. droppers every 3-6 ft; bungee snoods help crabs hold on.
Bait: chicken necks (cheap, keep fresh/cold), salted eel or bull lips (tough, last longer), razor clams in mesh.
Set in 5-15 ft along a drop-off or channel edge, roughly parallel to shore. Start upwind/uptide.
Drop the first anchor, pay out slowly in a straight line, stretch tight, drop the second anchor.
Marking buoys: same color/size/shape both ends, 12 in.+, with your DNRid.
Run it: idle up to the buoy, lift line onto a roller or U-arm, creep along at the slowest speed.
Line should rise at ~30-40 deg. Too fast? Drag a bucket or drogue.
Netter at the bow; scoop up from under/behind the crab before it lets go. Don't shade the line.
Wait 15-20 min between runs; rebait as you go.
Stay inside legal hours and 100 ft from other gear; pull gear before 5 p.m. in the Bay mainstem.
No license needed. Legal 24 hrs and on Wednesdays.
Tie a chicken neck to 10-15 ft of cotton or nylon line with a small sinker.
Toss several lines around pilings and the dock edge; tie off each.
When a line goes tight or moves off, pull hand over hand, slow and steady.
Ease the crab to just under the surface; slip the net under it from behind and scoop.
Use a wire/chicken-wire net; crabs tangle in nylon mesh.
No license needed. Walk shallows, grass flats or pilings at low light.
Net from behind; crabs bolt backward and sideways.
Watch pilings just under the waterline; crabs cling there.
License needed if 16+; up to 30 traps/rings combined.
Bait the center (razor clams, menhaden, chicken necks).
Drop to the bottom; soak 5-20 min.
Pull fast and steady so the sides close (trap) or the net bags (ring).
Buoy each one with your DNRid unless tied to the dock or boat.
Vary depths until you find crabs; rebait when washed out.
Register free with DNR each year (MD Outdoors, 410-260-3220).
Max 2 pots per property, within 100 yards of your shore.
Install a turtle reduction device in each entrance and keep cull rings open.
Mark with your DNRid; tie to the dock or buoy and sign it.
Bait the bait well (menhaden, razor clams, necks); check every day or two.
Unlicensed limits still apply: 2 dozen hard, 1 dozen peeler/soft.

where.tip: Crabs wake up as water warms into the mid-50s F and up; slow, often deeper. Traps and pots in deeper holes beat trotlines early (rule of thumb).
Crabs feeding hard; trotlines come on by late June. Work 5-10 ft on edges near grass beds and creek mouths.
Peak season. Early morning best in heat. Hot water and low oxygen can push crabs off the flats into slightly deeper, cooler water.
Heaviest, fullest crabs. Males move deeper (10-15 ft+) toward channel edges as water cools; fishing hours shorten. Season ends Dec 15.
Moving water beats slack; try the hour before high or low, best when it lines up with sunrise.
Soft mud bottom edges, drop-offs, oyster shell, grass beds, marsh banks, pilings. Shell bottom often produces on trotlines.
Males (jimmies) favor the fresher upper Bay and rivers; mature females move to saltier lower Bay to spawn.

handling: Grab from behind at the back swim fin, or use tongs and gloves.
Measure every crab, spike tip to spike tip, with a culling ruler. 5 in. until Jul 14, 5 1/4 in. from Jul 15.
Sex it: jimmy (male) = long narrow inverted-T apron (Washington Monument), blue claw tips.
Sally/she-crab (immature female) = triangle apron. Sook (mature female) = rounded dome apron, red claw tips.
Sponge crab = female with orange-to-black egg mass under the apron. Release gently right away.
In MD, every female goes back - hard or peeler. Doublers: keep the male only if legal, release the female.
Cull as you go: shorts and females back over immediately, near where caught.
Peeler sign: red line on swim-paddle rim. Soft crabs are fragile - handle gently.
Keep alive in a bushel basket, shaded, under a damp burlap or towel. Cool and damp, not wet.
Never in standing water or ice water - they drown. If on ice, keep a towel between ice and crabs.
Cook only crabs that are alive; toss dead ones.
Steam: rack over ~1-2 in. water + vinegar/beer, layer crabs with Old Bay or J.O.; lid on, about 20-30 min once steaming, until bright orange (check timing for size).
Conservation: take only what you'll eat; reset limits change yearly from the dredge survey.
